pronunciation.title: Say it right from day one

rules.explain: a=AH, e=EH, i=EE, o=OH, u=OO. Always. So CASA is KAH-sah.

examples.en: house
table

rules.rule: H is silent, J sounds like H
rules.explain: HOLA is OH-lah (no H sound). J in JUEVES sounds like English H: HWEH-vehs.

examples.en: hello
Thursday

rules.explain: Ñ is like NY in canyon: NIÑO = NEEN-yoh. LL and Y sound like Y in yes.

examples.en: boy
street

rules.explain: Tap your tongue once for R. PERRO (dog) rolls longer than PERO (but).

examples.en: but
dog

rules.explain: Most words stress the middle: HOLA = OH-lah, GRACIAS = GRAH-syahs. An accent mark (á) forces stress there.

examples.en: thanks
coffee

alphabet.title: The Ukrainian alphabet: 33 letters in Cyrillic
alphabet.explain: Ukrainian writes in Cyrillic with 33 letters, including Ґ (the voiced g) and І/Ї for the i-sounds. Two habits stand out: an apostrophe after і, ї or й before a vowel, and the soft sign ь that makes a consonant soft.

counting.title: Counting in Ukrainian: 0 to 15
counting.explain: Eleven and up: одинадцять, дванадцять, then тринадцять, чотирнадцять, п'ятнадцять — the number + настіє? the pattern is number + -наст(и)ть.
rules: The apostrophe marks і/ї/й before a vowel: п'ять (five), сім'я (family).
і is a real vowel (i as in machine) and it softens the consonant before it.
Щ is shch: щира (sincere) starts with the sh of ship plus a ch.
